name: Pathankot–Hanumangarh Highway
aka: Pathankot–Bathinda section was part of the former NH 15 (old numbering)
history: NH 54 runs down the western side of Punjab, from Pathankot at the foot of the hills to the sandy plains of northern Rajasthan. It follows the old NH 15 route through Amritsar, Faridkot and Bathinda, briefly clips the corner of Haryana at Mandi Dabwali, and ends at Kenchiya near Hanumangarh, where it joins NH 62.
facts: Starts on NH 44 at Pathankot and ends on NH 62 in Rajasthan.
Crosses the Sutlej river near Harike, home of a famous bird-rich wetland.
Passes through Amritsar, home of the Golden Temple.
Only a short stretch of about 38 km lies in Haryana, around Mandi Dabwali.
